comparator.academicYear: 2025-2026 Onderwijs- en Examenregeling (the most recent standalone formally adopted OER document accessible to available tools; no 2026-2027 OER was found through reasonable search), independently corroborated by the current official programme webpages checked 2026-09-27 for the Fall-2026 entrant cohort
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed primarily from the current formally adopted Onderwijs- en Examenregeling (OER) voor de Bacheloropleiding Gezondheidswetenschappen 2025/2026 (s7; decided by the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences decaan on 17 June 2025 after advice from the opleidingscommissie and consent of the faculteitsraad; Article 8.5 states it enters into force on 1 September 2025 and governs studiejaar 2025-2026), which is the most recent standalone formally adopted OER document accessible to available tools; no OER document specific to academic year 2026-2027 could be located through reasonable search of maastrichtuniversity.nl, and the only 2026-2027-dated document found (the Educatieve Minor/Module study guide, dated March 2026) is a different, minor teaching-qualification programme that itself still describes the 'richting Biologie en Gezondheid' as a linked pathway, corroborating that the OER's richting structure remains current going into the Fall-2026 entrant cohort. Its qualitative structure is independently corroborated by the current official Health Sciences overview and specialisaties pages (s0, s3, s4, checked 2026-09-27), which describe the same three recurring programme themes (Healthy Generations; Living Environment and Climate; Healthcare and the Social Domain) taught through the shared first year and the same biological/behavioural/environmental integration that the OER's richting structure formalises from year 2. Article 3.5 fixes the total study load at 180 ECTS. Article 3.6 and Bijlage 3 define the complete component structure: a shared, fully compulsory first year (60 EC: Een leven lang gezond 8, Bedreigingen van gezondheid 10, Gezondheid voeding en bewegen 8, Zorg(en) voor gezondheid 8; five block-bound skills units together 6; Introductie wetenschappelijke onderzoeksmethoden 6; Introductie statistische methoden voor data-analyse 5 plus its 1-EC study-group assignment; Filosofie-in-Actie 3; Training Introductie PGO 1; Schrijfonderwijs 3; Kwalitatief Onderzoek 1); Article 3.7 confirms the major carries 150 EC, of which a chosen richting's year-2/3 vakinhoudelijke blokken and blokgebonden vaardigheden, plus the shared Filosofie-in-Actie and Methoden, Technieken en Statistiek (MT&S) academische-vorming components, are compulsory, and that the major includes an afstudeerproject completed with an individual afstudeerscriptie (Article 1.2.l: 'een rapport waarin de student verslag doet van zijn afstudeerproject'); Article 3.8 fixes a genuine 30-EC minor (profileringsruimte) in year 3, chosen from the faculty's offer, which Bijlage 3 lists without prescribing its content, so it is preserved explicitly as unclaimed profiling space rather than instantiated with invented content. For the selected Preventie en Gezondheid richting, Bijlage 3 gives an explicit EC table for year 2 (60 EC: Uitdagingen in de Public Health 8, Planmatige Gezondheidsbevordering 10, Gezondheidsbescherming 4, Disease and Prevention 9, Public Health Policy 10, Public Health in International Context 5; six block-bound skills units together 8; the shared Filosofie-in-Actie sequence 6) and year 3 (60 EC: Implementatie van Public Health Interventies 6, Afstudeerscriptie 11; the shared Filosofie-in-Actie sequence including the afstudeerscriptie-linked reflection assignment 3; Voortgezette Statistiek en Methoden van Onderzoek 10; the 30-EC minor). Every component and its exact EC weight is taken directly from Bijlage 3's tables; the year-1, year-2 and year-3 subtotals each sum to exactly 60 EC as the OER itself structures them. Article 3.2 confirms voltijd delivery starting once yearly in September, matching the fixed Fall-2026 UCR cohort. No further official source needed to be consulted beyond the current overview/specialisaties pages used to corroborate the programme's general identity and confirm the route-selection basis: the current formally adopted OER alone already establishes a complete, internally consistent, entirely accounted-for 180-EC pathway with explicit EC and compulsory status for every component.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the Preventie en Gezondheid route of the Bachelor Gezondheidswetenschappen: a population-health core combining epidemiology, disease mechanisms and human physiology with the psychological science of health behaviour and health-promotion design, reinforced by the sociological, political and ethical study of health inequality and policy, and by introductory research methods, data analysis and persuasive health communication -- reproducing the route's own combination of disease prevention, systematic health promotion, health protection and public health policy, while leaving the 30-EC minor honestly preserved as unclaimed profiling space and the route's own supervised fieldwork/practical-skills training and afstudeerproject-based independent public-health research placement genuinely unmatched, since UCR offers no clinical/fieldwork placement or supervised thesis-length research project of that kind.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's biomedical/behavioural-science cluster (11 of 24: the two gateways Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine and Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Epidemiology & Public Health, Social Psychology, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Abnormal Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Infection & Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease and Human Physiology), reinforced by a governance/society cluster addressing policy and inequality (6 of 24: Law Society & Justice, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Introduction to Sociology, Modern Sociology, Qualitative Research Methodology and Ethics) and a light methods/economics/climate/communication thread (Research Methods & Statistics, Public Economics, Introduction to Data Science, Climate Change, Rhetorical Communication, Persuasive Communication). The label names disease prevention first for the dominant biomedical/epidemiological anchor, behaviour change second for the psychology cluster that implements systematic health promotion, and health policy third for the governance cluster, mirroring the Preventie en Gezondheid route's own combination of Uitdagingen in de Public Health, Disease and Prevention, Planmatige Gezondheidsbevordering and Public Health Policy.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by four generator-eligible programme-interest rows that specifically name healthcare and the social (care) domain (5518, 5972, a Stable study direction), designing healthy living environments (5529, a Direct programme interest) and sustainable and climate-resilient health systems (5531, a Direct programme interest), independently reinforced by the curricular-topic row healthy neighbourhoods and cities (5980): a concentration retaining only a light shared biomedical/data/communication anchor but replacing the closest match's disease-prevention, health-psychology and health-policy depth with UCR's full available Environment & Sustainability curriculum plus governance, rights and leadership coursework, studying how the physical living environment and the social and institutional organisation of care can be designed and governed sustainably to support population health, rather than studying disease prevention and health-behaviour change directly.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's Environment & Sustainability cluster (11 of 24: both sustainability gateways, Climate Change, R3: Recycling Recovery Remediation, Renewable System Design, Research in a Sustainable Delta, Building with Nature, Governance of Sustainability, Natural Hazards Risks & Adaptations, Environmental Biogeochemistry and Earth's Resources), reinforced by a governance/society cluster (5 of 24: Law Society & Justice, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Introduction to Sociology, Social Movements & Environmental Justice and Human Rights: Law & Philosophy) and a leadership/economics thread (3 of 24: Research Methods & Statistics, Leadership & Diversity Management, Public Economics), with a light shared health/data/communication anchor (Epidemiology & Public Health, Social Psychology, Introduction to Data Science, Communicating the Climate Crisis). The label names designing sustainable systems first for the dominant environment/sustainability cluster and socially resilient second for the governance, rights and leadership cluster that organises those systems around communities and institutions.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: The closest match already includes a light governance/society thread (Law Society & Justice, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Introduction to Sociology -- 3 of 24 courses) reflecting the route's own public-health-policy content, but this alternative goes materially further: it retains only a light shared biomedical/data/communication anchor (Epidemiology & Public Health, Social Psychology, Introduction to Data Science) -- 3 of 24 courses shared with the closest match beyond the shared governance thread -- but replaces 18 of the closest match's remaining courses (both HCB gateways, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Abnormal Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Infection & Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease, Human Physiology, Modern Sociology, Qualitative Research Methodology, Ethics, Climate Change's shared course aside, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Persuasive Communication) with UCR's full Environment & Sustainability curriculum (both sustainability gateways, Renewable System Design, R3: Recycling Recovery Remediation, Research in a Sustainable Delta, Building with Nature, Governance of Sustainability, Natural Hazards Risks & Adaptations, Environmental Biogeochemistry, Earth's Resources), Social Movements & Environmental Justice, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, Leadership & Diversity Management and Communicating the Climate Crisis. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from studying and preventing disease directly to designing and governing the sustainable physical and social infrastructure that supports population health, and the two alternatives share 10 of 24 courses while differing in 14 of 24 each way (105 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target (cp-000122, registry row 122, canonical_name 'Gezondheidswetenschappen', display_name_en 'Health Sciences', production_order 121, source_provider_id 113A920, programme_unit_code 1001O5913, recognized_programme_code 56553, languages_json=["NLD"], modes_json=["VOLTIJD"]) names no specific route. The current formally adopted Onderwijs- en Examenregeling (OER) for academic year 2025-2026 (s7, decided 17 June 2025, in force from 1 September 2025; Bijlage 3) confirms that after a shared 60-EC first year the major requires choosing one of five co-equal richtingen from year 2: Biologie en Gezondheid (biological mechanisms of health), Beleid, Management en Evaluatie van Zorg (policy, management and evaluation of care organisations), Digitale Technologie en Zorg (digital health technology), Geestelijke Gezondheidszorg (clinical psychopathology and mental-health care), and Preventie en Gezondheid (population-level disease prevention, health promotion, health protection and public health policy). Applying the Section 2.1 neutral route-selection hierarchy: Biologie en Gezondheid, Digitale Technologie en Zorg and Geestelijke Gezondheidszorg each commit to one narrow disciplinary, technical or clinical specialism (respectively human biology, digital-health engineering, and clinical psychopathology/diagnostics), and Beleid, Management en Evaluatie van Zorg is centred specifically on the administration and evaluation of care organisations. Preventie en Gezondheid instead studies population health through an integrated combination of biological, behavioural and environmental determinants (Uitdagingen in de Public Health; Disease and Prevention), health promotion and protection (Planmatige Gezondheidsbevordering; Gezondheidsbescherming) and health policy in a comparative/international frame (Public Health Policy; Public Health in International Context) -- the broadest, least specialised of the five richtingen and the one that most directly continues the shared first-year introduction to 'een leven lang gezond', 'bedreigingen van gezondheid' and 'zorg(en) voor gezondheid' without narrowing to one professional technique, organisation type or clinical population. The current official overview and specialisaties pages (s3, s4, checked 2026-09-27) independently describe the programme's own general identity as an integrated study of the biological, behavioural and environmental/social determinants of health, consistent with Preventie en Gezondheid's own scope rather than with any of the other four richtingen's narrower professional focus. Preventie en Gezondheid is therefore selected as the reconstructed route under Section 2.1's 'least specialised or most general route' branch of the hierarchy.

progressionAssessment.rationale: HCBGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes Human Physiology (semester 3), Infection & Immunity (semester 4) and Mechanisms of Disease (semester 6), all of which formally require it. HCBGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes Medical & Health Psychology (semester 3), Abnormal Psychology (semester 4) and Lifespan Developmental Psychology (semester 6), which formally require it. BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes Public Economics (semester 4), which formally requires it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Gateway and level-1/level-2 foundational courses (Epidemiology & Public Health, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Law Society & Justice, Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Data Science, Human Physiology, Introduction to Sociology, Foundations of Comparative Politics, Climate Change) are concentrated in semesters 1-3, and level-3 advanced work (Medical & Health Psychology, Public Economics, Infection & Immunity, Persuasive Communication, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Mechanisms of Disease) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match directly owns thirty-one generator-eligible rows describing the programme's own biological, behavioural, environmental and policy determinants of health, its methods training and its career/outcome framing (5514, 5515, 5516, 5519, 5520, 5521, 5527, 5528, 5530, 5533, 5534, 5535, 5536, 5965, 5966, 5967, 5968, 5969, 5970, 5971, 5973, 5974, 5975, 5976, 5977, 5978, 5979, 5981, 5983, 5984). These describe the programme's own general population-health, prevention, promotion and policy identity rather than an independent substantive direction, and are therefore substantively covered by the closest match's own core concept rather than forced into a residual candidate. The remaining four generator-eligible rows were independently assessed as one coherent candidate direction, 'Designing and Organising Sustainable, Socially Integrated Health Systems and Environments' (5518, 5529, 5531, 5972), reinforced by the curricular-topic row healthy neighbourhoods and cities (5980). This candidate passes all four gates: it is evidence-backed by four generator-eligible rows describing the design and organisation of healthy living environments and climate-resilient, socially integrated health systems, distinct from the closest match's disease-prevention-and-behaviour-change focus; it has a clear organising logic (the sustainable design and governance of the physical and social infrastructure that supports population health, rather than the study or prevention of disease itself); it is substantively distinct, replacing 18 of the closest match's 24 courses (135 EC) with UCR's own Environment & Sustainability, rights and leadership offerings, materially changing the alternative's academic priorities; and it is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with seven distinct level-300 courses and a pairwise difference of 14 courses (105 EC) against the closest match, comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course floor. Production therefore includes it as the second alternative. No further generator-eligible evidence remains to support a third genuinely distinct direction: every generator-eligible row is now owned by either the closest match or the second alternative, and no unclustered generator-eligible row or coherent combination of curricular-topic support-only rows remains available to organise an independent third concept without duplicating one of the two included directions or relying on an omnibus residual bucket. Production therefore stops at two alternatives and records insufficient-evidence as the stopping reason for a third.

notes.text: The Preventie en Gezondheid route combines biomedical, behavioural and policy training with hands-on practical-skills sessions and a supervised afstudeerproject culminating in an individual afstudeerscriptie. At UCR, students can approach population health through related disciplines such as biomedical science, health psychology, sociology and public economics, but UCR offers no supervised fieldwork placement, hands-on public-health practicum or thesis-length independent research project of that kind. Both UCR alternatives therefore offer related scientific, social and (for the second alternative) environmental-systems perspectives rather than reproducing the route's own practical and research-placement training.

The Preventie en Gezondheid route organises population health primarily around disease prevention, health promotion and public-health policy. The second UCR alternative instead organises related territory around the sustainable design and governance of the physical and social environments and systems that support health. The two programmes therefore cover related ground through substantially different curricular structures rather than one reproducing the other course by course.
